characters.description: The ruler of the Seelie Court, beautiful, ancient and precise. She grants audiences freely and gives nothing away without a price, and she prefers her prices to be paid in the form of something the payer will regret.
characters.name: The Seelie Queen

characters.description: The leader of the New York vampire clan, boyish in appearance and formally correct in everything he does. He observes the treaties scrupulously, which does not make him an ally, and he arrives at the Institute carrying news nobody wants to hear.
characters.name: Raphael Santiago

recaps.ending: The confrontation ends on Valentine's ship in the East River. He has taken four Downworlder captives, Simon and Maia among them, and completes the ritual that turns the Mortal Sword into a demonic instrument. Jace fights him; the Inquisitor Imogen, who had spent the book trying to destroy Jace, dies taking the blow meant for him, having finally accepted that he is not his father's creature. Simon is drained almost to nothing and revives by drinking Jace's blood, which leaves him a Daylighter, a vampire who can walk in sunlight, something no one has ever heard of. Clary draws an unfamiliar rune on the hull that tears the ship apart, and Valentine escapes into the water with the Cup and the corrupted Sword, leaving two of the three Mortal Instruments in his hands and only the Mirror unaccounted for. The survivors are pulled out of the river by Luke's pack. Maryse's suspicion of Jace is broken and he is welcomed back to the Institute; Clary and Simon have ended their attempt at a relationship, and what happened in the Seelie Court sits unresolved between Clary and Jace, who still believe themselves to be siblings. Jocelyn remains in her coma, and Valentine is stronger than he was.
recaps.in_short: Valentine is at large with the Mortal Cup, and Downworlder children begin turning up dead across the city, drained for a ritual. The Clave sends the Inquisitor Imogen Herondale to New York, convinced that Jace, as Valentine's son, is his father's spy; she imprisons him in the Silent City just as Valentine attacks it, slaughters the Silent Brothers and takes the second Mortal Instrument, the Mortal Sword. Jace escapes and shelters with Luke. Clary and Simon try to be a couple, but an audience with the Seelie Queen forces Clary to kiss Jace in front of him, and Simon walks away; shortly afterwards he is killed and rises as a vampire. The Inquisitor's attempt to trade Jace to Valentine collapses when Valentine shows he does not want him back. Valentine seizes four Downworlders, Simon and Maia among them, to complete a ritual aboard his ship. Clary destroys the ship with a rune of her own making. The Inquisitor dies saving Jace, Valentine escapes with the Cup and the Sword, and Simon, revived on Jace's blood, becomes a vampire who can walk in daylight.

recaps.text: Clary Fray grew up believing she was an ordinary Brooklyn teenager until she saw a demon killed in a nightclub and her mother Jocelyn was abducted the next day. She learned that she is Nephilim, a Shadowhunter, one of the angel-descended hunters who police demons and keep treaties with the Downworlder races, and that her memories had been repeatedly wiped by the warlock Magnus Bane at Jocelyn's request. Her father is Valentine Morgenstern, who once led the Circle in an attempt to purge Downworlders and overthrow the Clave, and who faked his death years ago. Clary recovered the Mortal Cup, the object that creates new Shadowhunters, but the Institute's tutor Hodge betrayed them and handed it, and Jace, to Valentine. At a ruined hospital on the river Valentine revealed that he had raised Jace as his own son under a false name, and that Clary is his daughter, so that Jace and Clary, who had begun to fall in love, believe themselves to be brother and sister. Valentine escaped through a Portal with the Cup. Jocelyn was recovered alive but comatose after drinking a potion to escape him, and lies in a hospital nobody can help her from. Clary's family friend Luke was revealed as a werewolf and a former Shadowhunter, Valentine's old sworn partner, and Clary's best friend Simon, an ordinary human, survived being taken by vampires.

Jace has moved out of the Institute. Maryse Lightwood has come back from Idris with her youngest son Max, and she can no longer look at the boy she helped raise without seeing Valentine's son; the Clave has ordered him watched. Clary is trying to live an ordinary life with her mother still comatose, training a little, and has begun dating Simon largely because the alternative is unthinkable. A faerie child is found murdered and drained of blood, the first of several Downworlder deaths that Downworlders are quick to blame on Shadowhunters. Jace picks a fight at a werewolf bar, where he meets Maia Roberts, a young member of Luke's pack. Then the Clave's Inquisitor, Imogen Herondale, arrives from Idris to conduct her own investigation. She has decided in advance that Jace is his father's agent, and she has him arrested and taken to the cells beneath the Silent City.

While Jace is held in the Bone City, Valentine attacks it. He kills the Silent Brothers, takes the second of the Mortal Instruments, the Mortal Sword, and leaves; Jace survives only because he is already in the cells, and walks out through the wreckage. Because the Clave now assumes he was complicit, he cannot go back to the Institute, and Luke takes him in. The murders of Downworlder children continue, the treaty between the Clave and the Downworlders comes under real strain, and the Inquisitor's grip on the investigation tightens rather than loosens. Clary and Jace keep colliding, unable either to be together or to leave each other alone, and Simon can see it happening.

Needing information about Valentine's plans, Clary, Jace, Simon and Isabelle go down into the Seelie Court. The Queen agrees to help, but sets a price: Clary must be kissed by the person she most desires. Clary tries to make it Simon, and it does not work; she kisses Jace instead, in front of everyone, and Simon watches. He ends their relationship on the way out, hurt but clear-eyed about what he has just seen. Shortly afterwards Simon is killed. Because of the vampire blood already in him from the attack a year earlier, he does not stay dead; he is buried, and Clary calls him out of the grave. He rises as a vampire, and has to work out at once what that means for his mother, his band, his school, and everything else he had been trying to keep.

Simon begins learning what he now is, hiding it from his family and refusing to join Raphael's clan. The Inquisitor decides that Jace's real value is as a bargaining chip and opens negotiations to hand him to Valentine in exchange for the Mortal Instruments, over the Lightwoods' objections. Alec, quietly, is spending more time than he can explain with Magnus Bane. Valentine's collection of Downworlder blood continues, and the pattern of the victims makes clear he is preparing a ritual rather than simply killing. Clary keeps producing runes that are not in any book, and nobody, including her, understands where they come from.

The Inquisitor's bargain collapses. Confronted with the offer of his son, Valentine makes it plain that Jace is worth nothing to him, and the Inquisitor's entire theory falls apart in front of her. Her interference has already weakened the Institute's protections, and demons get in. In the fighting a demon that feeds on fear moves through the building, and Clary invents a rune that makes a person fearless in order to face it. The Inquisitor, who has spent the whole book trying to destroy Jace, ends by defending him. Valentine, meanwhile, has what he needs to begin, and is waiting on the water.

Valentine's ritual requires the blood of one of each of the four Downworlder kinds. He takes captives to complete the set, Simon and Maia among them, and holds them aboard his ship in the East River. Luke's pack, the Lightwoods, Clary and Jace converge on the ship. Clary gets aboard and finds Simon barely alive; Jace goes after his father, and the Inquisitor makes her final choice, dying in Jace's place when Valentine strikes at him. Valentine completes the ritual and the Mortal Sword is turned from a heavenly weapon into a demonic one.

On the sinking ship Simon, drained almost to nothing, drinks Jace's blood and survives; it leaves him a Daylighter, a vampire able to walk in sunlight, which no one has ever heard of before. Clary draws a rune of her own making on the hull and the vessel comes apart around them. Valentine escapes into the water with the Mortal Cup and the corrupted Sword; only the third Instrument, the Mirror, remains unfound, and nobody knows what it is. Luke's pack pulls the survivors out of the river. Maryse's suspicion of Jace is broken and he is taken back into the Institute; Clary and Simon are no longer together; Jocelyn is still in her coma; and what happened in the Seelie Court sits unresolved between Clary and Jace, who continue to believe they are brother and sister.

characters.description: An LAPD homicide detective called to a Laurel Canyon property after a dog uncovers a human bone. The victim is a child buried for roughly two decades, and Bosch commits himself to recovering an identity and a history from the sparse remains.
characters.name: Harry Bosch

characters.description: Bosch's homicide partner. Edgar shares the long investigation from the canyon excavation through old missing-person reports, though he remains more attentive than Bosch to procedure and the cost of letting a cold case consume the team.
characters.name: Jerry Edgar

characters.description: A rookie patrol officer who responds to the discovery in Laurel Canyon. Older than most probationary officers and determined to prove herself in a second career, she begins a relationship with Bosch while remaining subject to close departmental scrutiny.
characters.name: Julia Brasher

characters.description: The lieutenant commanding Bosch and Edgar's squad. Billets must protect a delicate child-murder inquiry from leaks and premature conclusions while managing Bosch's attachment to both the case and a rookie officer connected to it.
characters.name: Grace Billets

characters.description: A boy who disappeared from his Laurel Canyon neighborhood in 1980. Once the recovered skeleton is connected to him, evidence of repeated healed injuries shows that his life had involved sustained abuse before his death.
characters.name: Arthur Delacroix

characters.description: Arthur's father, now an alcoholic living with the consequences of the family he damaged. He admits physically abusing his son, making him an immediate suspect when the old remains are identified.
characters.name: Samuel Delacroix

characters.description: Arthur's older sister and one of the last people to know his circumstances before he vanished. Her memories of their violent home and the neighborhood children help Bosch reconstruct Arthur's intended escape and final movements.
characters.name: Sheila Delacroix

characters.description: A neighborhood boy from Arthur's childhood whose skateboard becomes part of the reconstruction of the victim's last day. As an adult, Stokes is difficult to locate and gives Bosch reason to question the old account of Arthur simply running away.
characters.name: Johnny Stokes

characters.description: A former resident near the burial site whose history makes him a conspicuous early suspect. Public disclosure turns investigative interest into an accusation before Bosch has evidence tying Trent to Arthur's death.
characters.name: Nicholas Trent

characters.description: A forensic anthropologist who studies the recovered skeleton. His reading of age, old fractures, and fatal trauma turns scattered bones into a record of a child's abuse and gives Bosch the parameters needed to search old missing-person files.
characters.name: Dr. William Golliher

characters.description: A medical examiner who works with Bosch's team on the remains and the later physical evidence. Her conclusions help distinguish injuries suffered during Arthur's life from the blow that killed him.
characters.name: Teresa Corazon

characters.description: A Los Angeles Times reporter whose coverage can bring resources and witnesses to a cold case but can also make an uncharged person publicly synonymous with a child's murder. Bosch must manage what the department releases to her.
characters.name: Keisha Russell

recaps.ending: The skeleton is identified as Arthur Delacroix, whose many healed fractures record years of abuse by his father, Samuel, but the fatal event came from another child. Arthur had a skateboard connected to neighborhood boy Johnny Stokes; when Stokes confronted him in the hills, he struck Arthur and left him hidden in the canyon. Bosch proves Stokes's responsibility after first seeing suspicion and a press leak destroy Nicholas Trent, who was not Arthur's killer. During the final police action, rookie Julia Brasher mishandles her weapon and suffers a fatal self-inflicted gunshot. The department presents her death in a more heroic form and places blame on the suspect rather than acknowledge the accident. Bosch cannot accept a convenient official story after spending the case stripping away another set of convenient assumptions. With Arthur's killer identified but Trent and Brasher also dead, he decides that solving the homicide no longer justifies his place inside the institution. He hands over his badge and leaves the LAPD, ending the book as a civilian.
recaps.in_short: A dog finds a child's bone in Laurel Canyon, leading Harry Bosch and Jerry Edgar to a skeleton buried for about twenty years. Forensic examination shows repeated abuse, and old records identify the boy as Arthur Delacroix, who vanished in 1980. Arthur's alcoholic father admits beating him, while sister Sheila helps reconstruct a plan to run away. A leaked suspect name directs public blame at former neighbor Nicholas Trent, who dies before evidence clears him. The decisive trail instead runs through a skateboard and childhood acquaintance Johnny Stokes, who confronted Arthur in the hills, killed him, and concealed the body. Bosch solves the old murder, but the case produces a second institutional falsehood when rookie officer Julia Brasher, with whom he has begun a relationship, fatally shoots herself during police action and the department recasts the accident as heroism at a suspect's hands. Disillusioned by both needless deaths and the official response, Bosch resigns from the LAPD.

recaps.text: Previously: While Harry Bosch testified against filmmaker David Storey, retired FBI profiler Terry McCaleb investigated Edward Gunn's staged murder and was deliberately led toward Bosch as the suspect. They exposed the killing as a frame designed to discredit Bosch and collapse Storey's trial. Bosch was cleared and the prosecution survived, but he remained separated from Eleanor Wish and troubled by how plausible others found the idea that he might impose justice himself.

A dog brings home a human upper-arm bone from the wooded slope behind a Laurel Canyon house. Harry Bosch, Jerry Edgar, patrol officer Julia Brasher, and forensic specialists secure and excavate the site, uncovering the incomplete skeleton of a child buried for roughly two decades. Dr. William Golliher finds numerous healed fractures, evidence that the child endured repeated abuse over time, as well as trauma associated with the death. With no recent missing-person report to guide them, Bosch begins the slower work of estimating age and date, checking old records, and treating the forgotten victim as a homicide rather than an archaeological curiosity. He is also drawn to Brasher, a probationary officer who entered police work later than usual and wants to be judged on her present ability.

The forensic profile and old missing-child records lead Bosch to Arthur Delacroix, who disappeared from the Laurel Canyon area in 1980. Arthur's father Samuel is an alcoholic who admits he beat the boy, making the healed fractures understandable and placing him under immediate suspicion. Arthur's sister Sheila describes a household governed by violence and says her brother intended to run away. Bosch and Edgar still need to separate long-term abuse from the event that killed Arthur and to establish how the body reached the hillside. Their inquiries return to the people who lived nearby, including Nicholas Trent, whose past makes him easy to view as a threat to children even though the evidence has not tied him to this child.

Information about Nicholas Trent leaks before Bosch can complete the evidence check. Public attention converts a possible lead into an apparent accusation, and Trent dies under the pressure despite the absence of proof that he killed Arthur. The loss reinforces Bosch's distrust of conclusions driven by reputation rather than physical facts. Sheila's memories and the skeletal injuries point toward Arthur's last day, including a skateboard associated with another neighborhood boy, Johnny Stokes. Bosch begins searching for the adult Stokes and testing whether the fatal injury could have occurred in a confrontation among children rather than in the continuing abuse inside the Delacroix home. His relationship with Julia Brasher develops at the same time, though her probationary status and need to prove herself create risks neither can ignore.

Bosch finds that Samuel Delacroix was responsible for much of Arthur's suffering but not necessarily the final blow. The skateboard provides the missing route from Arthur's plan to leave home to Johnny Stokes, who had reason to follow and confront him in the hills. Stokes's present account does not fit the reconstructed injuries or the location of the grave. Bosch and Edgar build the old case through surviving memories and physical details rather than a confession preserved from 1980. Meanwhile the damage caused by the Trent leak cannot be repaired: even clearing him in the homicide does not reverse the public accusation or his death. Bosch becomes increasingly alert to the way police narratives can create a second victim when certainty outruns evidence.

The team establishes that Johnny Stokes confronted Arthur over the skateboard, struck him, and left the child concealed in the canyon. The solution explains the fatal trauma while preserving the separate truth that Arthur had suffered years of abuse from his father. Police move to secure Stokes and complete the case. During the resulting action, Julia Brasher's determination to perform as a full officer intersects with problems in how she carries and handles her weapon. A shot seriously wounds her, and the immediate police account favors an attack by a suspect over the possibility of an accidental discharge. Bosch sees another narrative forming before the physical evidence has been honestly faced.

Bosch closes the twenty-year-old homicide by proving that Johnny Stokes killed Arthur Delacroix during their childhood confrontation and concealed his body in Laurel Canyon. Samuel Delacroix's abuse explains the older fractures but not the death, and Nicholas Trent was wrongly transformed from a lead into a public suspect before his own death. Julia Brasher dies from the self-inflicted gunshot suffered during the final police action. The department shapes the account to make her a fallen hero shot by a suspect, avoiding the negligence and accident shown by the evidence. For Bosch, that choice repeats the case's central failure: protecting a satisfying story at the expense of the truth and the people damaged by it. Although Arthur finally has a name and a solution, Bosch no longer believes he can continue under the institution's terms. He turns in his badge and leaves the LAPD.

characters.description: A fifteen-year-old art student living in Brooklyn with her mother. She is small, red-haired, and stubborn, happier drawing than arguing, and has spent her whole life assuming she is entirely ordinary. On a night out at a Manhattan club she watches three armed teenagers kill a boy that nobody else in the room seems able to see, which is the first crack in that assumption.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Clary's best friend since childhood, a bookish, dryly funny teenager who plays in a struggling band with his schoolfriends. He knows nothing of any world beyond the ordinary one and follows Clary into trouble out of pure loyalty. His feelings for her have gone past friendship, which she has not noticed.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: A fair-haired boy of about seventeen, one of the three young hunters Clary sees at the club. Arrogant, quick with an insult, and unnervingly good with a blade, he treats hunting demons as both a duty and a sport. He is genuinely startled that Clary can see him at all, since ordinary people cannot, and that curiosity is what makes him take an interest in her.
characters.name: Jace Wayland

characters.description: A tall, dark-haired girl who hunts alongside Jace and her older brother, armed with a long electrum whip and willing to act as bait to draw a demon out of a crowd. Confident and theatrical, she enjoys the work and has very little patience for ordinary humans.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: Isabelle's older brother, dark-haired, quieter and far more cautious than either of his companions, and fiercely protective of Jace. He distrusts Clary from the moment she appears and resents the disruption she brings into their household.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: Clary's mother, a painter who has raised her alone and told her almost nothing about her own past. Calm on the surface and immovable underneath, she responds to Clary's account of the club by announcing that the two of them are leaving the city at once, and lets slip words that mean nothing at all to her daughter.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Jocelyn's oldest friend, a big, shabby man who runs a second-hand bookshop and has been a steady presence in Clary's life since she was small. When Clary comes to him for help after her mother disappears, he is inexplicably cold to her and sends her away.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: The eccentric woman who occupies the ground-floor apartment of Clary's building, reading fortunes from tarot cards and tea leaves amid a great deal of clutter and a very old set of curtains. She has known Jocelyn for years and clearly knows more about the family upstairs than a neighbour should.
characters.name: Madame Dorothea

characters.description: The tutor at the New York Institute, a greying scholar who trains its young hunters, keeps its library, and is rarely seen without his black bird. Learned and kind in a distracted way, he has not set foot outside the building in many years and shows no sign of wanting to.
characters.name: Hodge Starkweather

characters.description: One of the Silent Brothers, the order of archivists and lorekeepers who guard the Bone City beneath a Manhattan cemetery. His eyes and mouth are sealed with runes and he speaks directly into the minds of those around him. His order can search a person's memory as readily as a book, and their judgement carries weight with the Clave.
characters.name: Brother Jeremiah

characters.description: A Shadowhunter of the previous generation who founded the Circle, a movement that meant to purge the Downworlder races and then turned on its own government. His rebellion was put down years ago and he is believed to have died in a fire; older Shadowhunters still lower their voices when they say his name. He is hunting for the Mortal Cup, the object that can make new Shadowhunters, and he does not much mind who he has to go through to reach it.
characters.name: Valentine Morgenstern

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, a glittering, theatrical figure with cat's eyes who throws enormous parties for the city's Downworlders. Centuries old and expensively bored, he does nothing for free, remembers everything, and takes an immediate interest in the Lightwood brother who cannot look at him directly.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: A vampire of the New York clan who has the face of a boy of fourteen. Courteous, devout, and careful about the treaties that keep his kind and the Shadowhunters from open war, he would rather negotiate a problem away than fight over it.
characters.name: Raphael Santiago

recaps.ending: Hodge Starkweather, once a member of Valentine's Circle and cursed by the Clave never to leave the Institute, betrays the household: he takes the Mortal Cup from Clary and hands Jace over to Valentine in exchange for his freedom. Clary and Luke follow to a derelict building on the river, where Valentine reveals that he raised Jace as his own son under a dead man's name, that Jocelyn is his wife, and that Clary is therefore his daughter. Jace and Clary, who had just begun to fall in love, are told they are brother and sister, and neither of them is given any reason to doubt it. Valentine escapes through a Portal with the Mortal Cup; Clary shatters the mirror behind him so he cannot be followed. Jocelyn is recovered alive but locked in a coma of her own making, and is taken to a hospital where no ordinary doctor can help her. Simon has survived being turned into a rat and nearly drained by vampires; Luke's true nature as a werewolf and former Shadowhunter is out in the open; and Clary is left knowing exactly who her father is, with the Mortal Cup in his hands and her mother beyond waking.
recaps.in_short: Fifteen-year-old Clary Fray watches three teenagers kill a demon in a Manhattan club, an event nobody else can see, and within a day her mother is abducted and her ordinary life is gone. Taken in by the young hunters of the New York Institute, she learns that she is Nephilim, one of the Shadowhunters who police demons and Downworlders, and that her memories have been deliberately blocked for years. Her mother's disappearance is the work of Valentine Morgenstern, a Shadowhunter who once led a rebellion and now wants the Mortal Cup, the object that creates new Shadowhunters. Clary recovers the Cup from a tarot deck her mother painted, learns that her family friend Luke is a werewolf, and discovers a talent for creating runes nobody has seen before. Their tutor Hodge betrays them and delivers the Cup and Jace to Valentine, who reveals that he is father to both Jace and Clary. Valentine escapes with the Cup, and the two are left believing themselves to be siblings.

recaps.text: Clary Fray and her best friend Simon Lewis talk their way into the Pandemonium Club in Manhattan, where Clary watches three armed teenagers her own age corner and kill a blue-haired boy. Simon sees none of it, and when she reports it there is no body. The next day her mother Jocelyn is frightened and insistent that the two of them leave the city immediately, and mentions people and words Clary has never heard. Clary storms out. When she calls home that evening she hears a struggle, and her mother tells her not to come back and to call their old family friend Luke. She goes home anyway to find the apartment wrecked and her mother gone, and is attacked by a demon that she manages to kill with a device one of the club hunters had planted on her. Jace, the fair-haired boy from the club, arrives and takes her, wounded and half-conscious, to a converted church in Manhattan called the Institute.

At the Institute, Clary meets the Lightwoods, Alec and Isabelle, and their tutor Hodge Starkweather, and learns what the world actually contains: Shadowhunters, descended from an angel, who hunt demons with runed weapons under a body of law called the Clave, and Downworlders, the vampires, werewolves, warlocks and faeries with whom they keep an uneasy treaty. Clary is one of the Nephilim herself, and something has been blocking her memories for years. The Institute is attacked, which tells Hodge that Clary matters to somebody. Returning to her ruined apartment with Jace, she meets her downstairs neighbour Madame Dorothea, who knows far more about Jocelyn than a neighbour should. Luke turns Clary away coldly when she goes to him, and she overhears him speaking with two strangers about a man named Valentine and about the Mortal Cup, the object that makes new Shadowhunters, which they are certain Jocelyn has hidden.

Hodge explains the recent history: Valentine Morgenstern founded the Circle, a movement that meant to purge Downworlders and overthrow the Clave, and its uprising was put down years ago; Valentine is believed to have died in a fire, and Jocelyn was his wife. The Silent Brothers take Clary down into the Bone City to search her mind, and find a block placed by the warlock Magnus Bane. Clary and the others crash Magnus's party to demand answers, and he admits Jocelyn paid him to wipe her daughter's memories over and over. During the party Simon is briefly turned into a rat and carried off by vampires. Clary begins to piece together how much of her life was arranged for her, and to notice how easily she and Jace fall into each other's company.

The group raids the vampires' derelict hotel to get Simon back, arriving on a flying motorcycle and leaving with Simon alive but badly frightened, having been bitten. The vampire Raphael Santiago is careful to keep the incident from becoming a breach of the treaty. Clary's memories keep returning in fragments, and she works out that her mother would never have kept the Mortal Cup anywhere but close to hand. She and Jace grow closer, and on his birthday they end up alone in the Institute's greenhouse, where he tells her something of his childhood: his father was killed in front of him when he was ten, and he was raised afterwards by the Lightwoods. Simon, who has loved Clary for years, walks in on them.

Clary realises the Mortal Cup is inside a tarot deck her mother painted, and pulls it out of the card with a rune she invents on the spot, a talent nobody has seen before. Before they can leave, a greater demon rises in the apartment, using Madame Dorothea's body; Dorothea is killed and Jace is very badly hurt driving the thing off. Luke arrives with a pack of werewolves, and everything he had hidden comes out: he is a werewolf, and before that he was Lucian Graymark, a Shadowhunter, Valentine's closest friend and sworn partner. He tells Clary the rest of it, that Valentine survived, that Jocelyn took the Cup and ran, faking her own death, and that Clary's whole childhood was an act of concealment. Magnus heals Jace, and the Cup is finally in Shadowhunter hands.

Hodge, a former Circle member cursed never to leave the Institute, betrays them all. He takes the Mortal Cup from Clary and delivers Jace to Valentine to buy his own freedom. Clary and Luke follow to a ruined hospital on the river, where Valentine is holding Jocelyn, unconscious and unwakeable after drinking a potion to keep herself out of his hands. Valentine tells Jace that he is his true father, that he raised him under another man's name, and then tells them both that Clary is his daughter as well, so that the two of them are brother and sister. Neither is given any grounds to doubt it. Valentine escapes through a Portal with the Cup, and Clary destroys the mirror behind him. Jocelyn is carried out alive but comatose and taken to a hospital; Simon has survived; and Clary is left with a father she never knew, a brother she had been falling in love with, and a mother nobody can wake.

characters.description: An Elderling now rather than a Rain Wild outcast, keeper to the blue queen Sintara and one of the leaders of the settlement opposite Kelsingra. She hunts to feed the company, resists being told what she is for, and is warier than most of the keepers about what handling the city's memory-stone does to the people who do it.
characters.name: Thymara

characters.description: Keeper of the scarlet dragon Heeby, the first of the company to fly and, since then, the most confident person in it. He has begun immersing himself in the memories stored in Kelsingra's stone, and what he brings back with him is changing how he speaks, fights and looks at Thymara.
characters.name: Rapskal

characters.description: The former slave among the keepers, tending the green queen Fente. Steady and unglamorous, he is still in love with Thymara and still losing ground to a rival he does not know how to compete with.
characters.name: Tats

characters.description: The Bingtown scholar who came to study dragons and stayed, now the only person systematically recording an Elderling city as it is rediscovered. She is separated from Leftrin, who has taken the barge downriver, and afraid that her husband will find a way to reclaim her.
characters.name: Alise Kincarron Finbok

characters.description: The blue queen dragon, flying now and hunting for herself, restored enough to be magnificent and still short of what a dragon should be. She wants what the buried city was built to supply, and she is not inclined to explain herself to her keeper.
characters.name: Sintara

characters.description: The golden dragon whose plan brought the herd upriver, and the one most aware of how much of dragonkind's inheritance is missing. He knows what the city needs to be made to work, and how little time the herd has to find it.
characters.name: Mercor

characters.description: Rapskal's scarlet dragon, no scholar but the strongest flier in the herd, and the reason the keepers can reach the city across the river at all.
characters.name: Heeby

characters.description: Captain of the barge Tarman, gone downriver to collect the payment the Rain Wild Traders promised and the supplies the settlement cannot survive the winter without. He finds the councils at Cassarick a good deal less willing to honour a contract than they were to sign it.
characters.name: Leftrin

characters.description: Once Hest Finbok's secretary and dragon thief, now an Elderling bonded to the copper queen Relpda and settled with Carson. He is useful, changed and reasonably happy, and entirely aware that Hest will not have let the matter drop.
characters.name: Sedric Meldar

characters.description: The expedition's hunter, now the settlement's, keeping a village of young Elderlings and a herd of dragons fed in unfamiliar country. He is Sedric's partner and the closest thing the keepers have to a level-headed adult.
characters.name: Carson

characters.description: A Bingtown Trader's daughter transformed into an Elderling by dragon influence, once a spoiled girl and now a formidable negotiator with a claim to being the Rain Wilds' unofficial queen. She is married to Reyn Khuprus and has a small son whose health is failing in ways no healer can mend.
characters.name: Malta Khuprus

characters.description: Malta's husband, a Rain Wild Trader of the Khuprus family and an Elderling like her, who grew up among the buried Elderling ruins beneath Trehaug and knows more about their magic than most.
characters.name: Reyn Khuprus

characters.description: Malta's younger brother, an Elderling who spent years travelling as Tintaglia's ambassador and speaking for dragons to anyone who would listen. He is now a prisoner in Chalced, kept as a curiosity by a dying Duke who has been told that Elderling flesh and dragon blood can restore a man's youth.
characters.name: Selden Vestrit

characters.description: Alise's husband, a wealthy Bingtown Trader accustomed to arranging other people's lives. His comfortable existence has been invaded by Chalcedean agents who know exactly what he commissioned Sedric to bring back, and who are not asking politely.
characters.name: Hest Finbok

characters.description: A small silver dragon, spiteful, foul-tempered and the most damaged in memory of the herd, who spits venom at anyone within range and is disliked by dragons and keepers alike.
characters.name: Spit

characters.description: The great blue-silver queen who hatched in the buried city beneath Trehaug and bargained the serpents home, and who has since gone her own way. She has been flying the coasts of Chalced, where hunters have been paid a fortune for any part of a dragon.
characters.name: Tintaglia

recaps.ending: The keepers hold a city they cannot yet use. Kelsingra stands almost undamaged across the river, its stone full of preserved Elderling memory, but the magic that ran it depends on Silver drawn from wells that are no longer giving, and until the dragons get it they will remain less than dragons and unable to make proper Elderlings. Rapskal, steeped in the memories of a dead Elderling warrior, has become the loudest voice for taking up the city's inheritance wholesale, and Thymara is close to him and increasingly unsure who she is close to. Leftrin has recovered Tarman and secured supplies, but only by making enemies of the Cassarick council, which has no intention of honouring the expedition's contract and every intention of getting its own people upriver to claim a share. Hest, coerced by Chalcedean agents who know what he commissioned, is on his way north to find Sedric and the dragon parts he was promised. In Chalced, Selden Vestrit remains a captive of a dying Duke who has been told Elderling flesh will restore him. And Tintaglia, shot with poisoned Chalcedean weapons while hunting the coast, comes to Kelsingra in terrible condition, seeking the only creatures in the world who might be able to save her, and bringing the war over dragon parts directly to the keepers' door.
recaps.in_short: Settled opposite Kelsingra, the keepers can only reach the city on dragonback, and once there they find it nearly intact but inert: the Elderling magic that ran it needs Silver from wells that have stopped giving, and without Silver the dragons cannot become what they should be. Alise records and maps everything; Rapskal begins immersing himself in the memories held in the city's stone and returns from them carrying a dead Elderling's confidence and opinions, drawing Thymara after him. Downriver, Leftrin discovers that the Cassarick council means to cheat the expedition of its payment, and fights to get his barge and his supplies back. Hest Finbok's comfortable life collapses when Chalcedean agents demand the dragon parts he commissioned, and he is forced north to find Sedric. In Chalced, the dying Duke keeps Malta's brother Selden caged as a supposed cure, while Malta and Reyn's newborn son sickens beyond any healer's help. Tintaglia, hunting the Chalcedean coast, is struck down by poisoned weapons and arrives at Kelsingra gravely wounded, bringing the trade in dragon flesh to the keepers' doorstep.

recaps.text: Previously: the sea serpents of the Liveship Traders trilogy were dragons that could not complete their life cycle, and Bingtown's liveships had been built from stolen dragon cocoons. Tintaglia, the last dragon, hatched beneath Trehaug and bargained her protection of Bingtown for the Rain Wilders' help in guiding the serpents upriver. They came too late: in Dragon Keeper the clutch that hatched at Cassarick was stunted, flightless and unable to hunt, a burden the Rain Wild Traders were desperate to be rid of. The Traders' Council hired a company of heavily marked young outcasts as keepers and contracted Captain Leftrin's liveship barge Tarman to take dragons and keepers far upriver in search of the Elderling city of Kelsingra. Among them were Thymara, keeper to the imperious blue queen Sintara; the former slave Tats; the odd, fearless Rapskal and his small red dragon Heeby; and Greft, who meant to lead. Alise Kincarron came from Bingtown as the expedition's scholar, escaping a hollow marriage to the wealthy Hest Finbok, accompanied by Hest's secretary Sedric, secretly sent to steal dragon blood for the Chalcedean market. In Dragon Haven the journey remade them all: Sedric was bonded to the copper queen Relpda after she saved his life, his theft was exposed, the hunter running the same trade died for it, and Sedric changed sides and fell in love with the hunter Carson. Greft's attempt to found a new order among the keepers ended in his death. The dragons learned to hunt and then to fly, and the keepers finished changing into Elderlings. Alise and Leftrin became lovers. At last the company found Kelsingra, standing intact on the far bank of a river too wide to cross, and settled in a smaller Elderling village opposite it while Leftrin took Tarman downriver for payment and supplies.

Life in the village opposite Kelsingra settles into a hard routine of hunting, building and waiting. Only the flying dragons can carry keepers across the river, so access to the city is rationed by which dragons will consent to it, and Thymara, whose queen is proud and uncooperative, is often left behind. What the keepers find in the city is close to undamaged: streets, halls, baths and market squares, and stone that holds the recorded lives of the Elderlings who built it. But nothing works. The city was run on Silver drawn from wells that no longer give, and the dragons are blunt that without Silver they will stay less than dragons, and the keepers less than the Elderlings the city was made for.

Alise sets herself to mapping and recording Kelsingra properly, the work she has wanted all her life. Rapskal takes a different approach: he immerses himself in the city's memory-stone, living the recorded lives it holds, and comes back with a dead Elderling's skills, certainties and appetites layered over his own. He urges the other keepers to do the same, arguing that the Elderlings left their knowledge deliberately and that refusing it is waste. Thymara, drawn to the person he is becoming and disturbed by how little of the old Rapskal is left, has to decide how much of that inheritance she is willing to take on. Meanwhile the dragons begin to search the city for the wells in earnest.

Downriver at Cassarick, Leftrin runs into a council that has no intention of paying for an expedition it can call a failure, and that would rather send its own people to claim Kelsingra than honour a contract with a bargeman. He fights for Tarman, his crew and his cargo, discovers that the message birds carrying news up and down the river have been tampered with, and finds allies in Malta and Reyn Khuprus. In Bingtown, Hest Finbok's life comes apart: Chalcedean agents arrive who know precisely what he commissioned Sedric to bring back, and they make it clear the debt will be paid in dragon parts or in blood. He is forced to start north.

In Chalced, the Duke is dying, and his physicians have persuaded him that dragon blood and Elderling flesh will restore his youth, which has put a bounty on every dragon in the world. Selden Vestrit, Malta's brother and once Tintaglia's ambassador, is kept caged and displayed as a specimen of the cure. Malta and Reyn's small son is failing, and no Rain Wild healer can help him; Malta becomes convinced that only dragons can. Above the Chalcedean coast, Tintaglia is hunted with poisoned weapons by men who have been offered a fortune for any part of her. Wounded and unable to heal, she has nowhere to go but to the herd she abandoned.

The keepers cannot make Kelsingra work without Silver, and the search for the wells becomes the settlement's whole purpose. Rapskal's Elderling memories give him answers nobody can check and an authority the others resent, and he and Thymara become lovers on terms she is not certain of. Leftrin gets Tarman free of Cassarick and turns upriver with supplies, leaving behind a council that now regards him as an enemy and a rival claim on the city forming behind him. Hest, escorted north by people he cannot refuse, is coming to find Sedric. And Tintaglia, poisoned, torn and failing, reaches Kelsingra at last, bringing with her the certainty that Chalced will hunt dragons anywhere and the question of whether the herd can save one of its own.

characters.description: Sixteen, training seriously as a Shadowhunter for the first time and living with her mother again now that Jocelyn is awake. The war is over, her father is dead, and she is free to be with Jace; the difficulty is that Jace has begun avoiding her without explaining why.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Raised by Valentine, born a Herondale, and now living as a Lightwood at the New York Institute. He is not sleeping, he is training past the point of sense, and he is pulling away from Clary for reasons he will not give, convinced that whatever his father did to him before he was born has not finished with him.
characters.name: Jace Lightwood

characters.description: A vampire who can walk in daylight and carries a Mark that punishes anyone who harms him sevenfold, which makes him the most interesting thing in the city to several people he has never met. He is playing gigs with his band, dating Isabelle and Maia at the same time without either knowing, and no longer welcome in his own house.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: The Lightwood daughter, hunting regularly again and keeping her grief over her youngest brother behind a hard, flippant manner. She has started seeing Simon, on the understanding that neither of them is to take it seriously.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: Openly with Magnus now and travelling with him between assignments, which has given him time to work out that his partner is several centuries old and he is not. It is the first thing in his life he has had no idea how to fight.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, immortal, wealthy and in a relationship with a mortal teenager whose questions about his past he mostly deflects. He is called in whenever the Institute meets something it cannot identify, and he does not always say everything he knows.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: Clary's mother, awake after more than a year unconscious and rebuilding a life with Luke. She is uneasy about Jace in a way she cannot fully justify, because of what she saw Valentine do to a child once before, and she keeps things from Clary for what she considers good reasons.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Werewolf pack leader, bookshop owner, and about to marry Jocelyn. He acts as the city's Downworlder representative and is drawn into the investigation when Shadowhunter bodies begin turning up in ways that suggest a Downworlder killer and a deliberate provocation.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: A werewolf of Luke's pack, working at a Downworlder bar and studying when she can. She has been seeing Simon, does not know he is also seeing Isabelle, and does not talk about the boy who bit her and left her to become what she is.
characters.name: Maia Roberts

characters.description: A young musician who talks his way into Simon's band and then into offering him a room, at a point when Simon has nowhere else to go. He is friendly, evasive about his own history, keeps punishing training hours, and is clearly not telling Simon why he turned up when he did.
characters.name: Jordan Kyle

characters.description: A vampire of great age and beauty who led the New York clan before Raphael, and who has come back to the city with plans of her own. She has Simon brought to her, tells him he is being hunted, and offers him a place at her side in exchange for his loyalty.
characters.name: Camille Belcourt

characters.description: A small, shy girl who follows Simon's band and idolises him, and who is friends with the sister of one of the band members. She keeps turning up where Simon is, and he keeps failing to pay attention to her.
characters.name: Maureen Brown

characters.description: The veiled woman directing a cult that meets in a disused Brooklyn church, gathering followers who believe they are serving something greater and submitting to experiments in her name. She is far older than any demon the Shadowhunters routinely deal with, and what she is attempting has been tried before.
characters.name: Lilith

characters.description: Valentine's son by blood, given demon blood before he was born, who passed himself off as Sebastian Verlac in Idris and was killed at the end of the war. His body went into a river and was never recovered.
characters.name: Jonathan Morgenstern

recaps.ending: On the roof of a Manhattan building, Lilith completes the ritual she has been building all book: Jace, marked and controlled by her since the war, has supplied his blood, and Simon's is the last ingredient because it carries Jace's angel blood in it. Simon refuses to give it, and when Lilith strikes at him the Mark of Cain destroys her, throwing her attack back sevenfold. Clary breaks the rune that has been holding Jace and he is himself again for the first time in weeks. It is too late: the ritual has gone far enough. Jonathan Morgenstern, Valentine's son, wakes in the coffin Lilith prepared for him, and Jace, still bound to him by her work, leaves with him. The two vanish from the roof, and neither the Clave nor Clary has any idea where they have gone. Elsewhere, Camille Belcourt turns Simon's young fan Maureen into a vampire. Simon has lost his home and nearly lost himself; Alec has learned that Camille offered him something he had no business considering; and Clary is left standing on the roof with a ring in her hand and Jace gone, taken by the brother she watched die.
recaps.in_short: Six weeks after the war, Clary is training as a Shadowhunter, Jocelyn and Luke are planning a wedding, and Jace has begun avoiding Clary without explanation, tormented by dreams of hurting her. Simon, a Daylighter carrying the Mark of Cain, is thrown out by his mother, hunted by vampires who want to use him, and taken in by a werewolf named Kyle who turns out to be a guard assigned by the Praetor Lupus and, worse, the man who bit Maia. Camille Belcourt, the old head of the New York clan, tries to recruit Simon; Alec, worried about Magnus's immortality, secretly asks her for a way to make him mortal. Shadowhunters are being murdered and drained, and Clary traces the pattern to a cult repeating Valentine's demon-blood experiments on infants. Its leader is the demon Lilith, who has been controlling Jace through a rune and intends to raise Jonathan Morgenstern from the dead. On a rooftop, Simon's Mark destroys Lilith and Clary frees Jace, but the ritual has already worked. Jonathan wakes, and Jace, still bound to him, disappears with him.

recaps.text: Clary Fray grew up an ordinary New Yorker before learning she was a Shadowhunter and that her father was Valentine Morgenstern, who tried twice to overthrow the Clave and purge the Downworlder races. Valentine gathered the three Mortal Instruments and summoned the angel Raziel at Lake Lyn, killing Jace to do it; Clary had rewritten the ritual in her own name, so the angel answered to her instead, destroyed Valentine and granted her one request, which she used to bring Jace back. Before that, Jace and Clary spent two books believing themselves brother and sister, which turned out to be a lie of Valentine's. Jace is a Herondale, taken as a newborn and given angel blood; Valentine's true son, Jonathan, was given demon blood and grew up to pose as a Shadowhunter named Sebastian Verlac, kill Max Lightwood and betray Alicante to demons before Jace killed him on the battlefield. His body was never found. Clary's mother Jocelyn was woken from her coma and is with Luke, a werewolf pack leader who was born a Shadowhunter. Clary's oldest friend Simon became a vampire, then a Daylighter able to walk in sunlight, and carries the Mark of Cain, which turns any harm done to him back on the attacker sevenfold. The war ended with Downworlders seated on the Clave's Council for the first time.

Six weeks after the war, Simon is trying to hold together a life that no longer fits: his mother has found out what he is and reacted by calling him a monster, so he has left home; he is seeing both Isabelle Lightwood and Maia Roberts and has not told either about the other; and his band is playing small Brooklyn shows. Strangers keep approaching him and dying rather than answering questions, and vampires attack him more than once, protected only by the Mark he carries. Clary is training at the Institute and preparing for her mother's wedding to Luke. Jace has begun avoiding her, refusing to explain, sleeping badly and turning up at odd hours. Meanwhile a Shadowhunter's body is found in the city, drained of blood and left where it will be blamed on Downworlders.

A musician named Kyle joins Simon's band and offers him a spare room, which Simon takes because he has nowhere else. More dead Shadowhunters turn up. Simon is summoned by Camille Belcourt, the ancient vampire who led the New York clan before Raphael and has returned to the city; she tells him people are hunting him for his Mark and offers him a place beside her if he will help her take the clan back. He refuses to answer either way. Luke and the Institute try to keep the murders from breaking the new Accords. Jace, questioned by Clary, tells her only that he is dreaming of hurting her, and will not let her near him.

Kyle is revealed to be a werewolf, sent by the Praetor Lupus, an order that assigns guardians to newly turned Downworlders, and he has been assigned to Simon. Camille is captured with Magnus's help and held for the Clave, and while she is in custody Alec goes to see her alone; she offers to tell him how a warlock's immortality might be ended, which is the question he has not been able to stop asking about Magnus. Clary follows the trail of the killings to a disused church in Brooklyn where a cult calling itself the Church of Talto meets. In its basement she finds evidence of experiments on unborn children with demon blood, and a dead infant, which is exactly what Valentine did to his own son.

Kyle's full name comes out: he is Jordan Kyle, the boy who bit Maia and vanished afterwards, and Maia is not remotely willing to hear his apology. Simon's living arrangement becomes untenable and his double relationship collapses in front of both girls at once. Clary brings what she found in the church to Jocelyn, who tells her more about the experiments Valentine performed and about the child he raised on demon blood. Alec keeps returning to Camille without telling Magnus. The Shadowhunter murders continue, all of them tied to the cult, and the Clave still has no suspect.

Clary goes back to the cult's building and finds the woman who leads it, veiled and evasive, presiding over followers who have been giving up their unborn children to her work. The bodies in the basement are the failures. Investigating further, Clary finds a rune on Jace that neither of them put there, and learns that it has been on him since the end of the war. It explains the dreams, the withdrawal and the sleeplessness: he has not been himself, and whoever placed the rune has been steering him for weeks. Jace, understanding at last what has been done to him, tries to keep Clary away from what is coming, and cannot.

The woman is Lilith, greatest of demons, and the experiments in the church were rehearsals. Her real work is on the roof of a half-built luxury tower, where she has kept the body of Jonathan Morgenstern in a coffin surrounded by her runes. Jace has been her instrument, drawn to the site by the rune she set on him, and his blood, carrying the angel blood Valentine gave him, is part of the ritual. She needs one more thing: the blood of a Daylighter, because Simon's power came from drinking Jace's. Simon is taken to the roof, and Clary and Jace are there with him, one of them unable to act freely at all.

Simon refuses to give his blood. When Lilith attacks him the Mark of Cain reflects the blow sevenfold and destroys her. Clary breaks the rune binding Jace and he comes back to himself, but the ritual has already done what it needed to do: Jonathan Morgenstern wakes. He is alive again, Jace is tied to him by Lilith's work, and the two of them leave the roof together and disappear. Camille, still at large, turns Simon's young fan Maureen into a vampire. Alec's dealings with Camille come to light. Simon has lost his home and his mother; Maia and Jordan have started, cautiously, to talk; and Clary is left on the roof with Jace gone, taken by the brother she believed dead.

characters.description: Still barely trained, still inventing runes nobody has recorded, and now determined to reach the Shadowhunter homeland of Idris because a warlock there may be able to wake her mother. She has been told that Jace is her brother and has not found any way to make herself believe it in the part of her that matters.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Valentine's son by upbringing and, as far as anyone knows, by blood. He is going to Idris with the Lightwoods and is prepared to do almost anything to keep Clary out of the war, including deceiving her. He believes there is something wrong in him that his father put there, and he does not say so out loud.
characters.name: Jace Wayland

characters.description: Now a vampire who can walk in daylight, which makes him unique and therefore interesting to people he would rather not interest. He is still Clary's closest friend and still the person most likely to be arrested, exiled or used as leverage in a country where Downworlders are not welcome.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: A werewolf pack leader who was born a Shadowhunter, exiled after he was bitten, and has spent years keeping Jocelyn and Clary safe. Returning to Idris means returning to a country that threw him out, and to a Clave that will not want to hear what he has to say about arming Downworlders.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: The Lightwood daughter, travelling to Idris with her family as the Clave gathers for war. Capable, blunt and fiercely attached to her brothers, she is one of the few people who will say to Clary's face what everyone else is thinking.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: The eldest Lightwood child, still carrying his feelings for a warlock he cannot mention in front of his parents, and still the first to volunteer for anything dangerous. Idris is where his family's history and their old Circle membership are common knowledge.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: The youngest Lightwood, nine years old, brought to Alicante with the rest of the family. He reads constantly, notices more than the adults credit him with, and wants very much to be allowed to help.
characters.name: Max Lightwood

characters.description: Clary's mother, unconscious since she drank a potion to put herself beyond Valentine's reach. Everything Clary does in this book proceeds from the search for something that will wake her, and from the fact that the answers about her past are locked inside her.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Clary's father, holding two of the three Mortal Instruments and hunting the third. He has demanded that the Clave submit to him and is prepared to make his point with demons, which no Shadowhunter has ever been able to command before.
characters.name: Valentine Morgenstern

characters.description: Luke's older sister, who lives alone in a narrow house in Alicante and takes Clary in. She was married once to a Shadowhunter who left her, she stopped speaking to her brother when he became a werewolf, and she has kept a great deal of the previous generation's history to herself.
characters.name: Amatis Herondale

characters.description: A Shadowhunter of about Jace's age staying with the Penhallow family in Alicante, a cousin from the Institute in Paris whose own household was destroyed. He is charming, unusually helpful to Clary, an excellent rider and fighter, and interested in her in a way she finds flattering and slightly odd.
characters.name: Sebastian Verlac

characters.description: The Clave's new Inquisitor, appointed after his predecessor's death. He is genial in manner and ruthless in method, and his first significant act in the book is to decide what to do with a vampire the Clave never agreed to admit into Idris.
characters.name: Inquisitor Aldertree

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, found in Idris where Clary expected to find someone else. He is the only person likely to be able to brew what Jocelyn needs, he wants paying, and he is unusually reluctant to discuss his own history with Valentine's generation.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: The former tutor of the New York Institute, who betrayed Clary and Jace to Valentine in exchange for release from the curse that kept him indoors. He has been in Idris since, and knows more about the Mortal Instruments and Valentine's intentions than anyone else still alive.
characters.name: Hodge Starkweather

characters.description: An angel, held captive for years beneath the ruins of a country house and bound so that he cannot speak or free himself. He communicates in visions rather than words, showing what he has seen rather than explaining it, and what he has seen includes the experiments his captor performed.
characters.name: Ithuriel

characters.description: The angel from whom all Shadowhunters descend, who gave the first of them the three Mortal Instruments and has not been seen since. He can be summoned only by someone holding all three, at the lake where the first Nephilim were made, and he is bound to grant the summoner a single request.
characters.name: Raziel

recaps.ending: Valentine's rebellion ends at Lake Lyn, which is itself the third Mortal Instrument, the Mirror. He kills Jace there and uses the summoning to call the angel Raziel, expecting to be granted command of the Nephilim. Clary has already altered the runes of the ritual so that they name her instead, so the angel is bound to her, not to him. Raziel kills Valentine and grants Clary one request, and she asks for Jace's life; Jace wakes. On the battlefield Jace has already fought and killed the young man who called himself Sebastian, whose body falls into the river and is never recovered. In Alicante, Magnus uses the Book of the White to wake Jocelyn, who confirms what the angel's visions implied: Jace is not her son and never was. Valentine took him as an infant after his true parents, Stephen and Celine Herondale, died, and raised him under a dead man's name with angel blood in him. Jocelyn's own son, Jonathan, was the one Valentine fed on demon blood, and he was the boy passing himself off as Sebastian Verlac. Clary and Jace are not related. The Downworlders who fought under Clary's Alliance rune are given seats on the Council, Alec claims Magnus publicly, Max Lightwood is dead, and Simon goes home to New York still bearing the Mark of Cain.
recaps.in_short: Told that only a warlock in Idris can wake her mother, Clary follows the Lightwoods to the Shadowhunter homeland after Jace tries to leave her behind, and arrives by a Portal of her own making. In Alicante she is taken in by Luke's estranged sister Amatis, Simon is imprisoned for being a vampire on Shadowhunter soil, and she is befriended by a visiting Shadowhunter named Sebastian Verlac. Searching for the spellbook that will wake Jocelyn, she and Jace find an angel chained beneath Valentine's old country house whose visions reveal that Valentine experimented on unborn children with angel and demon blood. Sebastian sabotages the city's defences, kills the Lightwoods' youngest son and is exposed as Jonathan Morgenstern, Valentine's true son. Clary invents a rune that lets Shadowhunters and Downworlders fight as bound partners, and the Clave accepts the alliance. Jace kills Sebastian on the battlefield, and Valentine kills Jace at Lake Lyn to summon the angel Raziel, only for Clary to have rewritten the ritual in her own name. Raziel destroys Valentine and restores Jace. Jocelyn wakes and confirms that Jace is a Herondale, not her son, and that Clary and Jace were never siblings.

recaps.text: Clary Fray discovered she was a Shadowhunter after seeing a demon killed in a nightclub and losing her mother Jocelyn the next day. Her father is Valentine Morgenstern, who once led the Circle in an attempt to purge the Downworlder races and overthrow the Clave, and who faked his own death. Valentine took the Mortal Cup, then slaughtered the Silent Brothers to take the Mortal Sword and corrupted it into a demonic instrument aboard his ship, from which he escaped when Clary destroyed the vessel with a rune of her own invention. Only the third Mortal Instrument, the Mirror, is still unaccounted for, and nobody knows what it is. Valentine told Jace and Clary that he is father to both of them, so the two believe themselves to be brother and sister; Jace was raised by Valentine under another man's name and has been mistrusted by the Clave ever since the truth came out. The Inquisitor Imogen Herondale died defending him. Jocelyn lies comatose in a Manhattan hospital after drinking a potion to keep herself out of Valentine's hands. Clary's oldest friend Simon was killed and rose as a vampire, and after drinking Jace's blood became a Daylighter, able to walk in sunlight, which no vampire has ever done. Luke, once the Shadowhunter Lucian Graymark, leads a Manhattan werewolf pack and looks after Clary in her mother's place.

A former Circle member named Madeleine finds Clary and tells her that Jocelyn's coma is self-inflicted and can be undone, but only by a warlock living in Idris, the Shadowhunter homeland. Madeleine is killed before she can help further. The Lightwoods are being recalled to Alicante as the Clave gathers against Valentine, and Clary intends to travel with them, but Jace disables the Portal behind him rather than let her follow into a war. Clary makes her own Portal instead and comes through with Luke and Simon, falling into Lake Lyn on the way; the water of that lake is poison to Shadowhunters and leaves her ill and disoriented. Luke's estranged sister Amatis takes her in, and the reunion between Clary and Jace is furious on both sides.

Alicante is a city with demon-repelling towers and a hard rule against Downworlders, so Simon's arrival is treated as a crime. He is imprisoned in the Gard and questioned by the new Inquisitor, Aldertree, who starves him and offers to trade his freedom for testimony against the Lightwoods. Clary, staying with Amatis, is taken to meet the Penhallow family and is befriended by Sebastian Verlac, a Shadowhunter of her own age from the Paris Institute whose household was destroyed. He is charming and helpful, and Jace dislikes him immediately. The Clave debates Valentine's demand that it submit to him, and refuses to consider arming Downworlders.

Clary rides out with Sebastian to find the warlock who can wake her mother and discovers he is dead, killed by Valentine's demons; Magnus Bane is waiting in his place. Magnus tells her the antidote cannot be made without the Book of the White, a spellbook Jocelyn once owned, and that its last known location was Valentine's country manor. In the Gard, Simon shares a cell with a ragged prisoner who calls himself Samuel and who talks a great deal about the Mortal Instruments. Demons reach Alicante despite the towers, which should be impossible, and the Clave's confidence in its own defences begins to crack. Jace and Clary are alone together more than either of them can afford, with the fact of what they have been told about each other sitting between them.

Simon is got out of the Gard, and the prisoner who called himself Samuel turns out to be Hodge Starkweather, the Institute tutor who betrayed Clary and Jace to Valentine. Jace and Clary go to Valentine's abandoned country manor for the Book of the White. Following the dreams that have been troubling him, Jace finds an angel chained in the cellar beneath the house, held captive for years and unable to speak. The angel shows them both a series of visions: Valentine experimented on unborn children, giving one the blood of a demon and another the blood of an angel. Clary finds the Book of the White in the house. The angel is released and the manor comes down with him, and Jace is left with far more questions about himself than he had before.

Someone climbs Alicante's demon towers and disables the wards that keep the city safe. Max Lightwood, awake at night and quick to notice things adults do not, sees who does it, and is killed for it; his family finds him in the morning. Valentine's demons come through the failing defences in force and the city takes heavy losses. Valentine's terms are repeated to the Council: surrender the government to him, or be destroyed. Magnus has the Book of the White and can wake Jocelyn, but the Clave is in no condition to protect anyone, and the Downworlders, barred from the city and blamed for its troubles, have no reason to help.

Sebastian Verlac is exposed. He is not a Verlac at all: he is Jonathan Christopher Morgenstern, Valentine's true son, the child fed demon blood before he was born. He killed the real Sebastian Verlac and took his place, he brought down the towers, and he killed Max. He kills Hodge as well before he goes. Clary, working from what she can do that no one else can, invents a rune that binds a Shadowhunter and a Downworlder together as partners, giving each a share of the other's strengths. She takes it to the Council, and Luke brings the werewolves, vampires, warlocks and faeries to fight beside the Nephilim for the first time. Clary also marks Simon with the Mark of Cain, so that anyone who harms him suffers sevenfold. The Clave marches for Brocelind Plain.

The battle is fought by paired Shadowhunters and Downworlders, and it holds. Jace hunts down the young man who called himself Sebastian and kills him; the body goes into the river and is not recovered. Valentine takes Simon to Lake Lyn to complete the summoning, and finds he cannot spill the blood of a marked man without destroying himself, so he uses Jace instead and kills him. The lake is the third Mortal Instrument, the Mirror, and with all three Valentine calls the angel Raziel. But Clary has reached the ritual runes ahead of him and rewritten the name in them as her own. Raziel answers to her, kills Valentine, and grants her the one request the summoner is owed. She asks for Jace, and he wakes.

Magnus wakes Jocelyn with the Book of the White, and she confirms what the angel's visions implied. Jace is not her son. Valentine took him as a newborn after his true parents, Stephen and Celine Herondale, died, and raised him under a dead man's name with angel blood in him; Jocelyn's own son Jonathan, the one given demon blood, was the boy calling himself Sebastian. Clary and Jace are not related and never were. The Clave, having survived because of Downworlder help, gives the Downworlders seats on its Council and rewrites the Accords, and Alec Lightwood makes his relationship with Magnus public in front of all of them. Max Lightwood is buried in Idris. Simon returns to New York still carrying the Mark of Cain, and Jocelyn, awake at last, has her daughter back and a dead son she never speaks of easily.

characters.description: Seventeen, a trained Shadowhunter now, and the one thing her brother wants more than the destruction of the Clave. She carries a blade forged for her family generations ago, and the plan she eventually settles on depends on being close enough to Jonathan for him to believe he has won.
characters.name: Clary Fray

characters.description: Free of Lilith at last and carrying heavenly fire in his body, which he cannot control, discharge or safely touch anyone through. He is the only weapon anybody has that Jonathan's Endarkened cannot simply absorb, and learning to use it without killing the people around him is the whole of his life at the moment.
characters.name: Jace Herondale

characters.description: A Daylighter vampire, no longer protected by the Mark of Cain he traded away, and therefore as vulnerable as anyone else in a war between Shadowhunters. He is with Isabelle, banned from most of the places the fighting is planned, and determined to be useful anyway.
characters.name: Simon Lewis

characters.description: The last Lightwood daughter, hard and capable and openly with Simon now, which the Clave regards as another Downworlder problem. She has lost one brother already and has no intention of losing anyone else.
characters.name: Isabelle Lightwood

characters.description: Jace's sworn partner, leading missions and holding his family together while trying and failing to get Magnus to speak to him again. What he did behind Magnus's back is not something either of them has found a way past.
characters.name: Alec Lightwood

characters.description: The High Warlock of Brooklyn, no longer with Alec and still working with the Shadowhunters because the alternative is worse. He knows more about the realm Jonathan is drawing power from than he has ever admitted, for reasons that have to do with his own father.
characters.name: Magnus Bane

characters.description: Clary's mother, who has now watched her son destroy two generations of her family and is done hoping he can be reached. She gives Clary a Morgenstern blade she kept hidden for years, and tells her what it was made for.
characters.name: Jocelyn Fray

characters.description: Werewolf pack leader, Downworlder Council member, and the adult most likely to be shouted down in Alicante for saying that the Clave will need Downworlders again. He is recovering from wounds taken when Jonathan turned the first of the Endarkened.
characters.name: Luke Garroway

characters.description: Valentine's son, at the head of an army of Endarkened Shadowhunters and destroying Institutes one after another. He is unhurried about it. What he actually wants is not conquest in the ordinary sense, and it involves his sister.
characters.name: Jonathan Morgenstern

characters.description: A twelve-year-old Shadowhunter of the Los Angeles Institute, small, fair and already a serious fighter, who carries her family's ancient sword. She is closest to Julian Blackthorn, and she is present when Jonathan's forces come for her home.
characters.name: Emma Carstairs

characters.description: The second-eldest Blackthorn child of the Los Angeles Institute, about Emma's age and abruptly responsible for a houseful of younger siblings. Quiet, watchful and much steadier than a boy of twelve should have to be.
characters.name: Julian Blackthorn

characters.description: A werewolf of the Praetor Lupus, Simon's flatmate and guard, who has finally begun to repair things with Maia. The Praetor's house is one of the first places Jonathan's forces go looking for allies of the Clave.
characters.name: Jordan Kyle

characters.description: A werewolf of the New York pack, level-headed and increasingly the person the pack turns to while Luke is occupied with the Council and his injuries.
characters.name: Maia Roberts

characters.description: The Silent Brother who speaks aloud, older than he looks and connected to the Herondale and Carstairs families by a history he tells only in pieces. He is the closest thing the Clave has to an expert on heavenly fire, and he is the one who helps Jace live with it.
characters.name: Brother Zachariah

characters.description: The Consul, head of the Clave, running a war from a city filling with refugees. She is more reasonable than her predecessors and still bound by a Council that would rather blame Downworlders than change anything.
characters.name: Jia Penhallow

characters.description: A Prince of Hell and the ruler of the burnt-out demon realm Jonathan has been drawing on. He is courteous, exact and entirely transactional, he was already owed something before any of this began, and he is not in a hurry.
characters.name: Asmodeus

recaps.ending: The confrontation happens in Edom, the burnt demon world Jonathan has been drawing on. Jace's heavenly fire and Clary's Morgenstern blade are used together, and what they burn out of Jonathan is the demon blood Valentine gave him before he was born. For a few minutes what remains is the boy he would otherwise have been, frightened and ordinary, and he dies as that boy, in front of the mother and sister who had given up on him. His army of Endarkened cannot be restored and the war ends with them destroyed. Getting home costs more than the fighting did: Magnus's father Asmodeus, who rules Edom, sets his own price for opening the way, and Simon pays it, giving up his vampirism, his immortality and every memory of the Shadow World. He is returned to Brooklyn as an ordinary human who does not recognise any of the people he saved. Afterwards the Clave imposes the Cold Peace on the fair folk for their part in the war, which punishes those with faerie blood among the Nephilim as well. Brother Zachariah is restored to mortal life by the heavenly fire and reunited with the woman who waited for him; Magnus and Alec repair what Alec broke; Jocelyn and Luke marry; Emma Carstairs and Julian Blackthorn go back to Los Angeles bound as parabatai. In the closing pages Simon begins Ascension, and his memories start to come back.
recaps.in_short: Jonathan Morgenstern's Endarkened destroy Institutes across the world, and the Clave withdraws every surviving Shadowhunter to Alicante while Jace struggles to control the heavenly fire burning inside him. Among the refugees are Emma Carstairs and the Blackthorn children of Los Angeles. Jonathan takes hostages, the fair folk are exposed as his allies, and he offers terms that amount to a demand for his sister. Clary, Jace, Simon, Isabelle and Alec let themselves be taken to reach him, and cross into Edom, a dead demon world ruled by Magnus's father Asmodeus. There Jonathan is struck with heavenly fire and Clary's family blade, which burns the demon blood out of him; for a few minutes he is the ordinary boy he might have been, and then he dies. The Endarkened are destroyed with him. To open the way home Asmodeus takes his price from Simon, stripping away his immortality and every memory of the Shadow World and returning him to Brooklyn as a human who knows none of them. The Clave imposes a punitive Cold Peace on the faeries, and Simon, at the very end, begins to remember.

recaps.text: Clary Fray is the daughter of Valentine Morgenstern, who twice tried to overthrow the Clave and purge the Downworlder races and was destroyed by the angel Raziel. Her brother Jonathan was given demon blood before birth; he posed as a Shadowhunter called Sebastian, killed the youngest Lightwood child, betrayed Alicante to demons and was killed in the war, then raised from the dead by the demon Lilith. Jace, who is a Herondale rather than a Morgenstern and was given angel blood by Valentine, was bound to Jonathan by Lilith's ritual so that neither could be killed without the other, and spent months under Jonathan's influence while Clary infiltrated their household. Clary's friend Simon, a vampire who can walk in daylight, summoned Raziel and traded away the Mark of Cain for the sword Glorious; Clary used its heavenly fire to sever the bond and free Jace, and the fire remained inside him. Jonathan escaped, took an infernal cup made from Lilith's remains to an old sacred site, and forced a company of captured Shadowhunters to drink, turning them into the Endarkened: fighters who keep their training and lose themselves entirely.
